how: Members repeatedly call for help with the existing logo and its defence rather than only recruiting at its start.
AtomicEleven provides the recorded call and map that a neighbouring helper answers, without establishing who first placed the mark.
Members report expanding, moving and filling the logo while its design remains under discussion.
Anchor coordinates and corrected images turn the design into specific placement instructions.
Members negotiate spacing, blues, lettering and whether further alterations should proceed.
Posting a corrected template does not settle design unless participants also reconcile their differing interpretations and changing colour instructions.
Members ask for a decision before implementing a change and withdraw a competing proposal after agreement to preserve the existing design.
Small confirmations and thanks answer concrete design contributions without requesting a return.
The host help call receives a bare commitment from a participant identifying with a neighbouring school.
A local consultation rule is observed, but it cannot test cross-room prevalence or establish whether other governing arrangements existed.
The script exchange supports prospective adoption only because recommending automation and asking how to implement it do not establish execution.
A recommendation to automate upkeep prompts a request for the knowledge needed to write a script before any implementation is reported.
Claimed bot competition motivates a script recommendation, but the arrow must stop before executed automation or demonstrated exhaustion of manual capacity.
Replacement warnings and an explicit honour-based defence call mobilise protection of the existing logo.
A proposed protective lettering change is rejected when its mock-ups are disliked and obscure stripes participants value.
A direct correction identifies an apparent invasion as planned redesign, while a separate admission leaves some changes unattributed.
Correctly interpreting apparent damage depends on access to the shared redesign plan.
An attack warning requests support, a reply reports repair, and the answer thanks the helper while confirming reciprocal defence.
Members invite help for a neighbouring school, recall defending it, receive thanks and later credit its assistance.
Reciprocal defence reports and an appeal for neighbouring schools to stick together instantiate the smallest enacted alliance without establishing a shared hub or formal organisation.
Inter-room help includes proactive offers and reciprocal requests rather than requiring a prior declaration that the host lacks enough hands.
Mutual defence is observed, but early help and later cooperation reports do not establish when or why a coalition formed.
A participant carries the design discussion to the neighbouring subreddit without demonstrating an authorised diplomatic office.
Spacing and colour discussions establish design negotiation but supply no inter-room border agreement.
Neighbourly help is observed without an explicit refusal to attack, apology for damage or effort to restrain the room's attackers.
An upward logo adjustment is reported without establishing relocation after erasure or loss of the original spot.
Cooperation between neighbouring schools does not establish that one controls another's work as a territorial host.
The local decision-before-change procedure does not establish a dispute over who may bind the room to an inter-room agreement.
A design decision establishes neither an inter-room treaty nor an ensuing dispute over its representative.
Defence is visible without an evidenced transition into border negotiations.
The design and assistance passages do not establish a border agreement producing restraint.
An explicit request and repair establish help without showing that border bargaining opened its channel.
The upward adjustment does not establish insufficient hands causing abandonment of a lost spot.
Calls for help do not themselves establish a judgement that the room cannot hold its spot with its available hands.
The defensive honour claim identifies a canvas adversary but establishes neither a pre-existing rivalry nor a host attack.
Recalling earlier canvas vandalism does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
School colours and a preference for helping schools over colour factions do not establish a broader ideological or historical enactment.
The coded help call and design proposal supply no evidence of a host prank licensing deceptive claims.
Removing a competing design proposal to avoid confusion does not establish host-level containment of canvas discussion.
The help call and proposal withdrawal do not establish a canvas flood causing host-level posting boundaries.
The final-logo announcement celebrates shared effort and qualifies the result as almost perfect.
Closing reflections credit neighbouring helpers and describe the satisfaction of helping three schools.
A participant records a retrospective contrast between early conflict and better cooperation toward the end.
Reporting completion and celebrating it can occupy one title rather than two distinct events connected by a demonstrated causal transition.
A reply expands credit into retrospective description without establishing a separate decision to preserve the work.
Almost-perfect and bad-pixel judgements evaluate the ending without requesting cleanup or contesting which preserved version should represent history.
Closing reflections do not establish a decision to continue the effort through a later canvas, emblem or lasting organisation.
Retrospective accounts are present without an evidenced transition into deciding what collective effort to carry forward.
Participants enjoy a rival's takeover, mock damaged results and describe a poor finish as karma for earlier vandalism.
Temporal interpretation must follow concept times because the stock-taking theme contains pre-close rivalry alongside post-close celebration and reflection.
The short alteration suggestion has an unclear target, the explicit rival call is defensive, and another school's takeover is reported rather than claimed.
Mobilisation is observed without an established conversion into an offensive attack by the host room.
The ambiguous alteration suggestion does not establish a host attack followed by reasoned refusal or apology.
The ambiguous alteration suggestion does not establish an attack answered by a truce or border deal.
Retrospective contest talk can follow being targeted and defending a mark without an established preceding offensive attack by the host room.
A defensive call names the rival whose earlier vandalism is recalled in later contest talk, without proving that the call caused the judgement.
The call precedes work reports but those reports do not establish that the call recruited their authors.
The recorded call and map establish a gathering point without showing a distinct earlier initiating act that caused the call.
Construction and defence are observed without an explicit link showing that reporting a placed part caused later defence calls.
